newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Telewest focus on revenue, margins.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Telewest focus on revenue, margins.

text.p: British cable television and telephone operator Telewest Communications Plc is likely to show widening losses when it reports annual results on March 12 but interest will focus on its revenues and margins, analysts said.
"People will be watching for revenues per subscriber and its margins, the trend on telephony should be improving," said one analyst who asked not to be named.
The cable industry in Britain is still making investments to increase the number of homes which could access its services.
Around 11 percent of the population now take a product from cable, analysts said, with 31 percent of homes with access taking either
Telewest is expected to turn in a pretax loss of 165.5 to 246 million stg, compared with a loss of 114.7 million stg previously.
Loss per share should come in around 11.5 to 15.9 pence.
Telewest said in January that its customer base had risen nearly 34 percent with half of its clients taking both cable TV and telephone services.
It said then that telephone customers were up 45.5 percent over a year ago to 627,009 and TV customers totalled 528,142, up 31.5 percent.
Penetration rates for cable television in total are around 22.4 percent, analysts said, well ahead of satellite broadcaster BSkyB's 14.9 percent, although cable's subscriber base is smaller.
Analysts said Telewest's two-pronged offer of telephone and television was proving a success.
"It locks in subscribers more tightly, people are less likely to cancel if they have both TV and telephone services," the analyst said.

Telewest could also benefit in the future from an agreement announced on Friday with Bell Cablemedia and NYNEX CableComms to select an initial supplier of equipment to enable customers to receive digital services in cable homes.
"That could beat BSkyB and whoever enters the market first has an advantage," the analyst said.
BSkyB plans to launch digital satellite decoders in the autumn and has linked up with Carlton Communications and Granada Group to bid for digital terrestrial television networks.
"Telewest is marketing itself much, much better and the link-up announced on Friday means the industry is working together, that must be good news," the analyst said.
